keys.statement: Start a reactive column from a straight-line temperature profile between the bubble point at the condenser and the dew point at the reboiler for the mixed feed, constant molar flows, and a reaction extent peaking at the feed stage.

plain.title: Reactive column does not converge from defaults: start from straight-line temperatures and constant flows
plain.when: The reactive column solver fails from its default estimates.
plain.do: Start from a straight-line temperature profile between the bubble point of the mixed feed at the condenser and its dew point at the reboiler, with constant molar flows and a reaction extent peaking at the feed stage.
plain.why: Physically shaped profiles start the solver near a solution.
plain.check: Lab has not checked whether CHEPTA accepts such a starting profile; if not, start from a converged simpler case.

decisions.obstacle: The column solver does not converge from default estimates.
decisions.mechanism: Physically shaped profiles start the solver near a solution.
decisions.operation: Build the initial profiles this way.

keys.statement: Use the converged result of a simpler model, such as the column without reaction or with ideal K-values, as the starting point for the full reactive model.

plain.title: Full reactive model fails: converge a simpler model first and start from it
plain.when: The full reactive column model does not converge.
plain.do: Converge a simpler model first, the column without reaction or with ideal K-values (ideal vapour-liquid ratios), then use its result to start the full model.
plain.why: A simpler model gives profiles close to those of the full one.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, keep the simpler run and start the full run from it.

decisions.obstacle: The full model does not converge.
decisions.mechanism: A simpler model gives profiles close to the full one.
decisions.operation: Converge a simpler model, then switch the full model on.

keys.statement: Newton-type column solvers converge fast near the answer but fail from poor starting values or where several solutions exist; damping the Newton step (relaxation) widens the range from which they converge.

plain.title: Newton iterations diverge: improve the start or damp the step
plain.do: Improve the starting values, or damp the Newton step (relaxation) so it takes smaller moves.
plain.why: Full Newton steps overshoot far from the solution, and the method fails where several solutions exist.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, look at the solver's residual history: residuals that grow point to a poor start.

decisions.mechanism: Full Newton steps overshoot far from the solution.
decisions.operation: Improve the start or damp the step.

keys.statement: Homotopy continuation does not need good starting values but costs much more computation, because the modified system is solved many times; Newton or Broyden from good estimates is the better default.

plain.title: Homotopy continuation is robust but slow: keep it for cases with no good start
plain.when: A robust solving method is too slow for scans.
plain.do: Use Newton or Broyden from good estimates as the default; keep homotopy continuation (a chain of easier problems ending in the real one) for cases where no good start can be found.
plain.why: Continuation solves the modified system many times, so it costs much more computation.
plain.check: Time both methods on one case before choosing one for a scan.

decisions.obstacle: A robust method is too slow for scans.
decisions.mechanism: Continuation solves a sequence of problems.
decisions.operation: Keep continuation for cases where a good start cannot be found.

keys.statement: Reactive columns often have several steady states for the same inputs; find them by scanning a parameter or restarting from different initial estimates before accepting one.

plain.title: Reactive column converged but misses its target: look for other steady states
plain.when: A converged reactive column misses its target.
plain.do: Scan a parameter or restart from different initial estimates, and find the steady states before accepting one.
plain.why: Reactive columns often have several solutions for the same inputs (output multiplicity).
plain.check: In CHEPTA, record each branch found and which one meets the target.

decisions.obstacle: A converged reactive column misses its target.
decisions.mechanism: Output multiplicity: the same inputs give several solutions.
decisions.operation: Scan and restart from different estimates.
decisions.expected_change: All branches found, the right one chosen.

keys.statement: Rate-based (non-equilibrium) stage models are harder to converge than equilibrium-stage models and need reliable mass-transfer correlations.

plain.title: Rate-based column model fails: check the mass-transfer data and compare with the equilibrium-stage result
plain.when: A rate-based (non-equilibrium) stage model does not converge.
plain.do: Check the mass-transfer correlations, and compare with the equilibrium-stage result.
plain.why: Rate-based models have more equations with stiffer coupling than equilibrium-stage models.
plain.check: Converge the equilibrium-stage column first and use it as the reference.

decisions.operation: Check mass-transfer data; compare with the equilibrium-stage result.
